answers.reasoning: He admits he doesn't play accurately ('any one can play accurately') and reframes it as superior expression—recasting lack of skill as refined preference.
Lane neither denies nor apologizes; he coolly attributes the drinking to the wine's quality, deflecting the implied accusation with composure.
'I have only been married once. That was in consequence of a misunderstanding' is flat, understated, deadpan comedy.
He calls Lane's views 'lax' yet vows to forget his own marriage—condemning in Lane the laxity he professes.
Jack's 'Eh? Shropshire? Yes, of course' hesitation suggests he is concealing something that Algernon's probing threatens to expose.
Mock-grave language ('reckless extravagance') applied to tea cups and sandwiches creates comic disproportion.
Jack said he came for pleasure; Algernon retorts that proposing is 'business,' turning the quip against him.
'The very essence of romance is uncertainty'—he prizes suspense over fulfillment (acceptance ends the excitement).
'You behave as if you were married to her already. You are not'—Jack presumes a claim he hasn't won.
Algernon invokes the rule (reserved for Aunt Augusta) to deny Jack while eating them himself—self-serving enforcement of social rules.
Witty inversions (divorces made in heaven, lower orders setting example, romance as uncertainty) expose upper-class pieties about marriage as self-interest.
'spectre-gray' frost and 'weakening eye of day' establish cold, fading dusk with light/life draining.
Broken lyres = instrument that can no longer make music; emphasizes desolation.
Century's corpse, crypt, death-lament make the scene a funeral for the century.
Speaker leans on gate outdoors while all mankind has gone to household fires.
'Seemed fervourless as I' shows projection of his own lack of fervour onto the world.
'At once a voice outburst' interrupts the deathly scene with joy and vitality.
Aged, frail, gaunt, small, blast-beruffled—yet sings; joy despite frailty.
'Had chosen thus to fling his soul upon the growing gloom' — deliberate wholehearted offering against darkness.
'Shrunken hard and dry' vs 'full-hearted evensong' contrasts drained world with outpouring of feeling.
Hope 'whereof he knew / And I was unaware' — speaker lacks what the frail bird has.
'I could think there trembled' marks hope as tentative conjecture.
Ends on gap: bird knew, speaker unaware.
'So little cause for carollings... was written on terrestrial things' directly states nothing visible justifies the song.
Frail bird's ecstatic song vs deathly landscape; hope the speaker senses but is unaware of.
'Conscious of decent lives' and 'imperturbable faces' gazing at one another suggests complacent, watchful respectability.
Liking a book for the yellow leaves rather than content shows sensory/aesthetic response over substance.
Dark, muddy, dripping, odorous setting contrasts with boys' glowing play and echoing shouts.
She is lit by the doorway while the boys are in shadow; she becomes an idealized, illuminated figure.
Brother teases her casually; narrator stands silently gazing—silent fascination.
He watches from behind the blind so as not to be seen, then follows her daily—intent pursuit with concealment.
First person limits us to the boy's perception; she is seen only externally ('brown figure').
Retrospective narrator judges his younger self's passion as foolish—rueful hindsight.
'Her image accompanied me even in places the most hostile to romance' transitions her influence into the market scene.
Chalice metaphor casts his love as a sacred object carried through hostile crowd.
Admitted incomprehension invites readers to understand the unnamed adolescent feeling.
Body like a harp, her words and gestures like fingers on wires—he resonates to her slightest actions.
Religious imagery (chalice, prayers, litanies) against drab setting; girl becomes object of sacred devotion.
'Strange prayers and praises' directly links his infatuation to worship language.
